title: Must erasure and redaction be serialised with each other and with ledger commits?
current: `Graph.KG.Eraser` takes no ledger head lock; since 4.6.4 an erase made through an engine on a plain connection nests in the caller's transaction (aad50087), while an engine from `from_connect` runs it on a dedicated connection. `LedgerRedact.LiveRows` reads without locks. Probe [erasure_caller_transaction](receipts/native/erasure_caller_transaction_redaction.json): on a plain connection the erase nests at `$TLEVEL=1`, a concurrent redaction completes, and the caller's rollback restores the content ([bug-002](bugs_issues.md#bug-002)); through `from_connect` the erase [committed on its own](receipts/native/erasure_caller_transaction_from_connect.json) and the caller's rollback did not undo it.
working: Require committed erasure before redaction; treat caller transaction membership as unresolved rather than permitting dirty liveness reads.
options: (a) callers must not redact while an erase is uncommitted (document it); (b) redaction must refuse while any erase of the target is uncommitted (take the head lock in the eraser, or a shared target lock); (c) erasure must never join a caller's transaction.
settles: A maintainer statement choosing the contract and scope, or an existing attributable source that explicitly selects it; implementation behavior alone cannot decide intent.

title: Should another tenant's retry of a revision it shared with a redacted tenant be refused?

The valid mode-on native fixture in [weighted-native.json](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-9/weighted-native.json) has ekey0/weight10 and ekey5/weight1, plus a two-edge alternative of cost4: both native path and cost-only routes return4, whereas the whole stored multigraph has a cost1 path. [Independent source/intent review](../uplift/consolidated/iteration-9/weighted-projection-review.md) distinguishes this from the earlier mode-off harness-oracle miss. Plausible answers: define weighted paths over the lowest-key projection for compatibility, stating that graph to callers; or optimize over all parallel rows, changing the reader…

options: Preserve the current compatibility behavior or adopt the stronger intended alternative described in the canonical question; their observable difference must be tested.
settles: A maintainer statement choosing the contract and scope, or an existing attributable source that explicitly selects it; implementation behavior alone cannot decide intent.

title: Should an engine that cannot read the schema record be refused?
current: A readable record naming another schema refuses the engine on first access (IVGSchemaError). If reading ^IVG.Deploy raises anything else, the engine logs a WARNING and is accepted unchecked, so an engine for another schema can run in the namespace. title: Should setup save the schema record when the class deploy failed or was turned off?

title: What does a Python read with no graph argument read?

title: In a multigraph, does a direct edge delete remove one parallel edge or all of them?
current: delete_edge(s, p, o, graph=g) deletes every row of the triple in g (all parallel edges) and the ^KG entry, returning True. There is no edge_id/ekey argument. A single parallel edge can be deleted only through Cypher DELETE r. Evidence: live: intent-a-hd0202-multigraph-delete; inspected: iris_vector_graph/_engine/nodes_edges.py:1382-1433

title: May a direct edge delete remove an edge row that a temporal edge still implies?
current: delete_edge(s, p, o, graph=g) deletes the triple's rows whether marked ({"temporal":true}) or adopted, and their ^KG entries. title: How should erase and rebuild retire a source generation?
current: Erase paths (RemoveSource, RemoveGraph, RemoveAll) and the non-indexed rebuild kill ^KG("gen") with ^KG("degc"); later writes restart the counter, so it returns to earlier values. Adj.Degree stores a recount only if its lock probe succeeded and gen is unchanged, then re-reads gen. Live: gen 2 before erase, undefined after, 2 again after rewriting the same edges, on both erase_graph and delete_node; single-process degree answers stayed correct. The cross-process window (probe before the writer's lock, count after the kill, with tGen=0 or an ABA refill) was not exercised live. Evidence: live `intent-a-hd0401-gen-return`; inspected `iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Adj.cls:55-90`; inspected `iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Adjacency.cls:376-377,437,461,824-830`

options: - A: keep the kill and document the narrow window (erase/rebuild concurrent with degree readers) - B: step the generation with $Increment and kill only degc (a residue counter per erased source remains) - C: keep the kill, add a graph/namespace epoch stepped by every kill to each entry and to the reader's check
settles: A maintainer statement that erase/rebuild require no concurrent degree readers (A becomes the documented contract), or that erasure must leave no per-node residue (rules out B, leaves C).

title: May two adjacency rebuilds run at the same time?
current: Two ^KG rebuilds are admitted concurrently (shared lock only); two ^NKG rebuilds are serialized by ^IVG.NKGBuild (wait up to NKGBUILDWAIT=900 s, then raise). Not observed: the end state of two overlapping ^KG rebuilds. Non-indexed path: each kills and refills ^KG in its own transaction; an IRIS rollback of one restores pre-images (killing nodes the other set) - IRIS premise, not checked here. Indexed path: two %BuildIndices over the same index - IRIS behaviour not established. Evidence: live `intent-a-hd0402-two-rebuilds`; inspected `iris_src/src/Graph/KG/TraversalBuild.cls:30-70,281-303`

settles: A maintainer statement that sync() is an operator action assumed single-flight (A documented), or a test/proof that two overlapping BuildKG runs (one rolled back) leave ^KG equal to the rows.

Evidence: live `intent-a-hd0501-temporal-endpoints`; inspected `iris_src/src/Graph/KG/Adjacency.cls:575-613`; inspected `iris_src/src/Graph/KG/LedgerApply.cls:613-641`

Replay/reconstruct/verify ignore temporal records and the temporal index. title: Must a BM25 Build (and Drop) exclude writers and be all-or-nothing?
current: Build: `Kill ^BM25Idx(name)`, then per-document writes with no lock and no transaction, header and `schema=2` last; neither Build nor Drop takes the writer lock or checks `upgrading`. Live (intent-a-hd0701-build-drop-lock): with the lock held by process A, B's `bm25_insert` waited 2.0 s and raised "locked by another writer" (FR-019 holds), B's `bm25_build` returned in 1 ms and `bm25_drop` in 0 ms (index gone under a held writer lock). `bm25_build(idx, [" "])` passes `BM25BuildInput`, kills the complete previous index and returns `indexed 0` with no header (`Info` `{}`, search `[]`).

Model the as-built (unlocked Build/Drop, Kill-first) separately as the baseline. Same as decisions.md.
options: 1. Build and Drop take the writer lock and set a "building" flag that refuses writers (Search answers unavailable). 2. Build under a temporary name and swap it in under the lock (old generation stays visible; crash leaves the old one). 3. Keep today's behaviour with a documented, testable premise: no other writer on that index while Build/Drop runs.
settles: A maintainer statement scoping ADR-0007 to Insert/Delete (then alternative 3 with a documented quiet-index premise), or an ADR/FR naming Build and Drop.

Evidence: live: intent-a-hd0801-strict-cypher-window; run: intent-a-hd0801-unit-ledger-guard; inspected: iris_vector_graph/ledger/guard.py:20,38-80; inspected: iris_vector_graph/_engine/query.py:2299-2300
working: Take the contract text as intended: strict refuses with no window.
